acceptance_criteria.criterion: The "Add Repository" form includes a "Store" dropdown when multiple stores are configured, and the dropdown does not appear in single-store mode
Selecting a store in the dropdown sends the corresponding store_id in the API request
The "Conflicts" tab displays cross-store repository conflicts with clear winner ("Active") and shadowed indicators
The "Conflicts" tab shows a badge with the conflict count, hidden when zero
The "Move to Store" and "Remove from Store" actions resolve the displayed conflict

summary: Implemented store-aware UI components in the Strategy page (vanilla JS, no build step).
Added getStores() and getStoreConflicts() to api-client.js consuming GET /api/stores and GET /api/stores/conflicts.
In strategy.js: multi-store mode detection (stores.length > 1) gates both the tab bar and the Store dropdown on the Add Repository form.
Conflicts tab renders conflict cards with Active/Shadowed badges, vision summary, last-modified date, and Remove/Move action buttons for shadowed entries.
Conflict badge on the tab header updates reactively via updateConflictBadge() — shown only when count > 0.
resolveConflict() performs sequential deletion across all N store copies, then re-creates in the target store using the winner entry as canonical data.
Move to Store shows an inline store picker with Cancel fallback; Remove from Store resolves in one click.

All 5 acceptance criteria verified via live browser testing: Store dropdown visible only in multi-store mode, store_id sent in POST, Active/Shadowed indicators correct, badge shows/hides reactively, both resolution actions resolve the conflict and refresh the tab.

comments.note: In wireConflictActions() (strategy.js), the inline picker uses document.getElementById('move-store-sel-' + repoName) where repoName is read from a data-attribute. Repository IDs are slugs so this is safe today, but the ID selector would silently fail if a future ID contained characters that are invalid in CSS selectors (e.g. dots). Using querySelector('[id="..."]') or a data-attribute lookup would be more defensive.

In visionSummary() (strategy.js), the magic number 57 (= 60 - 3 for the ellipsis) is unexplained. A short inline comment ('// 60 chars - 3 for ellipsis') or a named constant MAX_VISION_PREVIEW_LEN would make the intent immediately clear.

resolveConflict() uses a recursive deleteAll() helper to remove N copies sequentially, relying on the server's guaranteed 'delete winner first' semantics. This is correct given the current API contract, but a brief JSDoc comment explaining the invariant would help future maintainers understand why sequential (not parallel) deletion is required here.

The createRepo JSDoc in api-client.js still lists 'vision' but not 'store_id' in the @param description for the data object. Since store_id is now a supported (and meaningful) field, adding it to the JSDoc would keep the documentation accurate.

summary: All 5 ACs verified via code review against implementation in api-client.js (getStores/getStoreConflicts additions) and strategy.js (Store dropdown + Conflicts tab). AC-1: isMultiStore guard (stores.length > 1) controls tab bar and dropdown visibility. AC-2: form submit reads new-repo-store element value and adds store_id to payload when present. AC-3: Conflicts tab renders badge-complete/badge-archived classes based on isWinner flag per entry. AC-4: updateConflictBadge() hides badge element when count=0, shows with count text when count>0. AC-5: resolveConflict() sequentially deletes all N registry copies then recreates in targetStoreId using winner entry data; refreshConflicts() re-fetches and re-renders without full page reload. 3,838 backend tests pass.

comments.note: strategy.js: all 5 ACs verified via code review (Developer confirmed live browser testing). The vanilla JS GUI has no automated unit tests — this is expected for this codebase's frontend layer. The critical logic paths (multi-store guard, store_id payload injection, badge show/hide, resolveConflict sequential delete + recreate) are all clearly implemented and correct.

strategy.js wireConflictActions(): inline picker uses document.getElementById('move-store-sel-' + repoName) where repoName comes from a data-attribute. Repo IDs are slugs (alphanumeric/hyphens/underscores) which are valid in CSS selectors, so this is safe today. Developer also flagged this — low risk.

strategy.js resolveConflict(): sequential deleteAll() has no timeout or max-retry. If a delete call fails mid-sequence, the error is displayed but the sequence stops, leaving the repo in an intermediate state (partially deleted). This is an acceptable limitation given the current usage scale, but worth noting for future robustness.

summary: No blocking issues found. Implementation is clean, follows established patterns, and correctly implements all 5 ACs.
Multi-store gating via `isMultiStore = stores.length > 1` is a clean, deterministic guard applied consistently to tab bar, Store dropdown, and Conflicts tab rendering.
XSS protection is solid — every piece of user-supplied data passes through `escapeHtml` before HTML string insertion, throughout both `buildConflictsHtml` and the inline store picker.
`conflictsIndex` and `storesSnapshot` in-memory caches are a correct and efficient pattern for event-delegation without DOM traversal.

`resolveConflict` JSDoc correctly documents the sequential-deletion invariant (delete-promotes-winner semantics). The recursive `deleteAll` error path correctly shows the error and stops recursion without false-success.

Two Fix-Forward changes applied: (1) inline comment `/* 60 chars - 3 for ellipsis */` added to `visionSummary` magic number 57; (2) `store_id` added to `createRepo` JSDoc @param description in api-client.js.

Low-priority observation: `getStoreConflicts()` is called on every Strategy page load regardless of store count. The server returns `[]` immediately in single-store mode, so the cost is negligible, but lazy-loading it after `getStores()` confirms multi-store mode would eliminate the unnecessary round-trip.

comments.note: strategy.js visionSummary(): added inline comment `/* 60 chars - 3 for ellipsis */` next to the magic number 57. Purely explanatory — no behavioral change.

api-client.js createRepo() JSDoc: added `store_id` to the @param data description (`id, label, folder_names, vision, store_id`). The parameter was already supported and sent by the form submit handler — this just makes the documented contract accurate.

strategy.js renderStrategyList(): calls `API.getStoreConflicts()` unconditionally on every page load via `Promise.all([..., API.getStoreConflicts()])`. In single-store mode the server returns `[]` immediately, so cost is trivial, but the call is unnecessary. A two-phase fetch (getStores first, then conditionally getStoreConflicts) would eliminate the extra round-trip for single-store users. Not blocking — the current approach is correct and the cost is negligible.

strategy.js wireConflictActions(): the inline store picker sets `id='move-store-sel-' + escapeHtml(repoName)` in innerHTML, but the subsequent `getElementById` call uses the raw `repoName` (already HTML-escaped from the data-attribute). For current slug values (`[a-z0-9_-]`) `escapeHtml` is a no-op so this is safe. If slug constraints ever relax, the mismatch would silently break Move to Store. Flagged by Developer and QA — acceptable given current invariants.
